Read the transition probabilities of a fit

Source: R/tidy-accessors.R
transition_probabilities.Rd

transition_probabilities() returns the transition probabilities of a fit, one row per ordered pair of states. The transition probability \(P(\text{to} \mid \text{from})\) is the share of the transitions leaving a state that go to each other state, so the probabilities out of one state sum to 1. They describe where the process goes next, regardless of chance expectation; the adjusted residuals of transitions() say which of these moves are more or less frequent than independence predicts. Together with the initial-state probabilities of initial(), they are the parameters of the first-order Markov model read by Transition Network Analysis.

A cell declared a structural zero has probability 0, as does every cell of a state that is never left.

Usage

transition_probabilities(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
transition_probabilities(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
transition_probabilities(fit)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa(), or a grouped fit from lsa(..., group = ).

Value

A data.frame with one row per from -> to pair (K^2 rows for K states, ordered by from and then to) and the columns from, to and prob. A grouped fit stacks the groups under a leading group column.

See also

initial() for the initial-state probabilities; transitions(), which also carries prob; lsa_to_tna().

Examples

transition_probabilities(lsa(engagement))
#>         from         to       prob
#> 1     Active     Active 0.69756839
#> 2     Active    Average 0.26747720
#> 3     Active Disengaged 0.03495441
#> 4    Average     Active 0.20372836
#> 5    Average    Average 0.60985353
#> 6    Average Disengaged 0.18641811
#> 7 Disengaged     Active 0.12000000
#> 8 Disengaged    Average 0.39692308
#> 9 Disengaged Disengaged 0.48307692
